Mina / team — preliminary triage notes after looking at logs and runtime traces: 

Observations:
- A subset of connections shows continuous byte-level activity on the TCP socket, but the token-streaming layer reports an idle period (no emitted chunks) for ~12–25s before tokens resume.
- The runtime's batching window was recently adjusted (May 10) to be more aggressive for cost reduction on long tail requests. That change shortens our internal flush boundary when prefix cache hits occur.
- Some front-door proxies (third-party customer infra) have 15s idle detection and will forcibly reset websocket connections if no TLS-level heartbeat occurs. If the runtime doesn't emit small periodic frames within that window the proxy resets the connection — client reconnects but misses the intermediate chunk sequence => UI shows a gap.

Hypothesis: batching + quieter token emission patterns for certain prompts cause gaps that trip proxy idle timers. Sentinel (our connection watchdog) currently waits 30s to alert but the proxy cut happens earlier. So the observed "sentinel timeout" in their logs is likely the proxy detected disconnect; our retried stream resumes but with missing continuous chunks.

Immediate remediation options (fast -> slower):
1) Server side: temporarily enable micro-heartbeats (single-byte PING frames / lightweight 0-byte chunks) emitted every 10s for affected model routes. This is a config flip we can push as a hotfix.
2) Client side: ask BrightLeaf to extend proxy idle to 30s for websocket origins used for streaming.
3) Longer term: adjust batching heuristics to avoid silent windows for interactive sessions, and add sequence glue to allow stream resumption without visible gaps.

I'll prepare a hotfix PR for option #1 and a rollback plan. ETA to push a canary: ~60–90 minutes after sign-off.

Connor O'Brien
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
